extraction.name: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS)
extraction.description: A large multilingual corpus suitable for speech research, derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox, consisting of 8 languages including about 44.5K hours of English and a total of about 6K hours for other languages.
extraction.creator: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert
extraction.inLanguage: English, German, Dutch, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Italian, Polish
extraction.citeAs: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert. MLS: A Large-Scale Multilingual Dataset for Speech Research. arXiv:2012.03411v2, 2020.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox. Downloaded using data preparation tools available at LibriLight open source library.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Training data is lower than available LibriVox data because text sources for audiobooks could not be downloaded, candidate labels were filtered during transcript retrieval (WER > 40%), or data was filtered while creating valid/test splits. Some links for text sources were invalid or redirected.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Read audiobooks from LibriVox and corresponding text from Project Gutenberg and other domains (gutenberg.org, archive.org, ccel.org, hathitrust.org).
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: Numbers in the matched text from the book are replaced with the corresponding aligned words from the pseudo label to handle variations in spoken numbers and page numbers.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Audio files segmented into 10-20 second segments based on silence intervals using Viterbi token sequences. Audio downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text normalization: NFKC normalization, removal of unwanted characters (punctuation, emojis, etc.), removal of end-of-line hyphenation, filtering characters outside valid unicode range for the language. Transcript retrieval: splitting source text into overlapping documents, TF-IDF matching with pseudo labels, Smith-Waterman alignment, filtering candidates with WER > 40% compared to pseudo labels. Heuristics applied for hyphens and apostrophes.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Pseudo labels generated via beam-search decoding with a 4-gram language model on acoustic models. Original transcripts retrieved by matching pseudo-labels to book transcripts. Human evaluation performed on development and test sets where transcribers listened to audio and corrected 'clear and obvious' errors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: WER between generated transcript and human rated transcript measured (e.g., English Dev 4.55%, Test 4.54%). Transcribers asked to correct only 'clear and obvious' errors to avoid adding potential bias.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Time-Depth Separable (TDS) Convolutions acoustic models, wav2letter@anywhere framework, 4-gram language model, TF-IDF, Smith-Waterman alignment algorithm.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Promotes open research in large-scale training of ASR systems and multilingual ASR. Opens new avenues in ASR and Text-To-Speech (TTS) research.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: English is the most dominant language (44.5K hours vs 6K total for others). Development and test sets are balanced for gender and duration, but training set may not be.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Pseudo labels may not always have correct transcription, affecting number replacement. Dealing with hyphens and apostrophes relies on heuristics. High OOV rate for Polish (13%) negatively impacts WER. Training data is lower than available raw data due to filtering.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) training, testing, and validation; Text-To-Speech (TTS) research; Low resource training; Multilingual ASR.
